primary_question: Can Chipotle grow its restaurant base and customer relationship while keeping store economics strong?
core_answer: Chipotle owns almost all its restaurants and combines a simple visible-food promise with digital ordering, Chipotlanes, and new-store growth. The main risk is that the cost of serving each customer is rising while existing-store traffic is only beginning to recover.

source_discovery_audit.what_it_found: FY2025 annual report, Q1 2026, Q2 2026, Q4 2025 results, and SEC company facts.
Annual report describes the menu, Food with Integrity, guest access, and accessibility goals; standalone offer pages need a later pass.
Digital sales, Chipotlanes, restaurant technology, and technology investment are described in filings and investor materials.
Q1 and Q2 releases capture Recipe for Growth, hospitality, menu innovation, Rewards, and group occasions; call transcripts remain a follow-up.
No outside operator source was added in this first pass; labor and customer checks are required next.
No campaign, product-drop, or unusual customer behavior source was added in this first pass.
McDonald's and existing affordability, ritual, workflow, and burden-carrier pages provide the first comparison frame.

mechanisms.name: visible food promise
mechanisms.what_happened: Customers choose ingredients and see food prepared in front of them.
mechanisms.first_principles_read: Visibility can reduce uncertainty and support a higher price.
mechanisms.what_to_verify_next: Repeat visits, complaints, food-safety trust, and price tolerance.

mechanisms.name: simple menu
mechanisms.what_happened: The business sells a narrow group of customizable meals.
mechanisms.first_principles_read: A narrower menu may make training and quality control easier.
mechanisms.what_to_verify_next: Order time, error rate, waste, and labor minutes per order.

mechanisms.name: Chipotlane
mechanisms.what_happened: Most new Q2 stores included a dedicated digital pickup lane.
mechanisms.first_principles_read: Easier pickup can widen the useful reach of one store.
mechanisms.what_to_verify_next: Sales, margin, and payback versus similar stores without a lane.

mechanisms.name: company-owned stores
mechanisms.what_happened: Chipotle owns and operates almost all restaurants.
mechanisms.first_principles_read: The parent keeps the store upside and carries the operating downside.
mechanisms.what_to_verify_next: Store margin, labor pressure, rent, and new-store returns.

mechanisms.name: digital ordering
mechanisms.what_happened: Digital sales were 38.3% of Q2 food and beverage revenue.
mechanisms.first_principles_read: Digital ordering removes some customer effort but can add kitchen and delivery work.
mechanisms.what_to_verify_next: Total visits, order size, labor minutes, errors, and delivery cost.

mechanisms.name: new-store growth
mechanisms.what_happened: Chipotle opened 100 company-owned restaurants in Q2.
mechanisms.first_principles_read: New stores can grow profit if each store earns back its build cost.
mechanisms.what_to_verify_next: Construction cost, ramp time, mature sales, and cash return by group of stores opened in the same period.

operating_evidence.claim: FY2025 comparable sales fell 1.7%, with transactions down 2.9% and average check up 1.2%.
Q2 2026 comparable sales rose 2.2%, with transactions up 1.0% and average check up 1.2%.
Q2 2026 restaurant-level margin fell to 25.2% from 27.4%, while food and labor costs rose as percentages of revenue.
Digital sales were 38.3% of Q2 food and beverage revenue, and 80 of 100 new Q2 stores included Chipotlanes.
FY2025 operating cash flow was $2.114B against $666.3M of capital spending and $2.426B of share repurchases.

investment_read: Chipotle has a credible growth engine, but the investment depends on new stores earning strong returns while existing-store traffic and margins recover. The company-owned model makes both the upside and the burden visible in Chipotle's own results.

deep_questions.question: Are new Chipotle stores adding demand or moving customers from older stores?
deep_questions.why_it_matters: A larger store count is valuable only if it adds sales instead of dividing the same local demand.
deep_questions.evidence_needed_next: Sales by store age, nearby store openings, trade-area overlap, and mature-store returns.
deep_questions.working_answer: We do not know yet. The opening pace is strong, but local cannibalization is not visible in headline revenue.
deep_questions.what_would_weaken_it: Older stores near new openings lose traffic while total company sales rise mainly from the new units.

deep_questions.question: Do Chipotlanes create better returns or just faster pickup?
deep_questions.why_it_matters: A lane is worth building only if the extra access produces more profit after construction and labor cost.
deep_questions.evidence_needed_next: Comparable new-store sales, margin, payback, and order mix with and without Chipotlanes.
deep_questions.working_answer: They likely help access, but the return claim still needs store-level proof.
deep_questions.what_would_weaken_it: Chipotlane stores have similar sales and margins after their extra build cost.

deep_questions.question: Did the return to positive transactions repair the customer relationship?
deep_questions.why_it_matters: One or two positive quarters may be a pause, while a lasting return would support the growth plan.
deep_questions.evidence_needed_next: Transactions through several quarters, repeat visits, price changes, and repeat-customer data by group.
deep_questions.working_answer: Q1 and Q2 show early recovery, but not yet a durable habit.
deep_questions.what_would_weaken_it: Transactions turn negative again when price increases or promotions change.

deep_questions.question: Does digital ordering help the whole store?
deep_questions.why_it_matters: Digital sales can grow while kitchen work, mistakes, delivery fees, and labor costs also grow.
deep_questions.evidence_needed_next: Order time, labor minutes, accuracy, pickup wait, delivery mix, and profit by order type.
deep_questions.working_answer: Digital ordering removes customer friction, but the store may carry more work.
deep_questions.what_would_weaken_it: Digital share grows while service quality and restaurant margin fall.

deep_questions.question: Will customers keep paying for the food-quality promise?
deep_questions.why_it_matters: Chipotle's brand depends on customers seeing enough value in fresh ingredients to return at a higher price.
deep_questions.evidence_needed_next: Transactions by price tier, customer income, menu mix, food-safety trust, and repeat visits after price changes.
deep_questions.working_answer: The promise still attracts customers, but Q2 margin and traffic data show a price limit must be tested.
deep_questions.what_would_weaken_it: Customers trade down, reduce visit frequency, or return only after discounts.

deep_questions.question: Is management expanding faster than it can train and staff stores?
deep_questions.why_it_matters: The store is the product. Weak training can damage speed, accuracy, food quality, and trust.
deep_questions.evidence_needed_next: Manager vacancies, retention, training time, service measures, complaints, and older-store performance.
deep_questions.working_answer: The risk is real because the company plans hundreds of openings while labor cost is rising.
deep_questions.what_would_weaken_it: Service and retention improve while the store base grows rapidly.

deeper_insights: Chipotle's advantage is a controlled store system that turns food preparation into part of the customer experience.
The company-owned model makes growth more demanding than McDonald's franchise model because Chipotle carries the labor and food pressure itself.
Positive transactions are more meaningful than revenue growth, but two positive quarters do not yet prove a lasting return.
Digital ordering is a change in where work happens, not proof that the work became easier.
Chipotlanes may be a physical growth tool as much as a digital tool because they widen the useful access to a store.
Food quality supports pricing only while customers still believe the meal is worth the price.
New-store growth can hide weak older-store behavior, so results by store age matter more than total restaurant count.
The clearest McDonald's contrast is that Chipotle owns the operating burden and keeps the operating result.
disconfirming_tests: Transactions turn negative again while average checks rise.
Chipotlane stores do not earn better sales, margin, or payback after their extra construction cost.
Older stores near new openings lose traffic and profit.
Digital sales rise while labor minutes, errors, delivery cost, or customer wait rise faster.
Restaurant-level margin stays below prior levels even after transactions recover.
Manager turnover or service failures rise as the store base expands.
